newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah softens, swaps ease on liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah softens, swaps ease on liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah softened against the dollar and swap rates also declined in early trading on Tuesday on the back of ample liquidity, dealers said.
"The market is liquidity-driven. Operators are a little bit surprised by the ample conditions," a local bank dealer said.
Dealers said operators seemed to be well prepared to face the new bank reserve requirement rate on Wednesday, helped by central bank injection of 847 billion rupiah on Tuesday.
One currency dealer in Singapore said trading in the spot market was dull and added the focus was on the swap market.
"The first reaction on central bank supply was forward selling. People think it might be the same again tomorrow, so they started selling in response," the dealer said.
He said six-month swaps fell to 71.5 from 74.0, but expecting strong support at the 70.0 level. "I don't have a clear view for the market at present. But I would buy on dips."
The dealer said declines in short-term swaps were also caused by some weakening in one-to-five-year swaps.
The local bank dealer said spot rupiah rose to a high 2,403.80 from an opening of 2,403.75/04.25 before softening to 2,405.0/05.2 at 0300 GMT.
Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,404.0/04.5 and 2,403.75/04.25, respectively.
Overnight swap edged down to 0.15/0.25 from 0.45/0.50 and tom/next to 0.38/0.43 from 0.48/0.50 points.
One Japanese bank dealer said offshore players were seen buying back at low levels after they initiated early selling.
One-month swaps were at 12.5/13.5, two at 24.5/26.5, three at 36.0/38.0 and six at 71.0/73.0 points.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,400/2,592 and the conversion band to 2,400/2,448 on Monday.
